newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea SEC finds price manipulations on Sam Yang.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea SEC finds price manipulations on Sam Yang.

text.p: South Korea's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said on Wednesday three people had been found by the body to have manipulated prices of Sam Yang Heavy Machinery Co shares earlier this year.

The commission has asked state prosecutors to probe the case, in which two investors and one employee of a local brokerage firm were found by the body to have violated market regulations, an SEC statement said.

The SEC said Sam Yang's share price had risen to a high of 47,500 won per share by early March from around 39,000 won in late February. It said its findings had shown the rise reflected a manipulation of the shares in the market.
The SEC said it has asked the prosecution to investigate two investors in the stock.
It said it has asked Daishin Securities Co to bring heavy punishment to the manager of the brokerage firm's branch in southern Seoul for cooperating with the two investors.
Sam Yang shares traded at 45,000 won in the morning session on Wednesday, up 800 won from the previous close.
The two investors and Daishin Securities could not immediately be reached for comment.
